exposure: state-level variation in antenatal care standards
state-level variation in access to health services
outcome: causes of full-term infant mortality (SUDI, congenital malformations, perinatal conditions, SIDS, suffocation)
cohort: The study included 10,175,481 infants born full-term in the US between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2012, identified using linked birth and death records.
finding: The overall full-term infant mortality rate in the US was 2.2 per 1,000 live births, with significant state-level variation, and Sudden Unexpected Death in Infancy (SUDI) accounted for 43% of these deaths, particularly SIDS and suffocation.
